mainTopic: Reducing wrongdoing with כלאים, and whether money from עבודה זרה in a גוי's hand is permitted
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא: one may not help tend כלאים, but one may help uproot them to reduce wrongdoing. It first assumes the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who says even keeping כלאים earns lashes. From that it proves רב נחמן's ruling that reducing wrongdoing is allowed. The proof is rejected, because the ברייתא may follow the רבנן. The גמרא then explains the ברייתא as dealing with free work, following רבי יהודה, and the support for רב נחמן returns. Next comes a new question: does money from selling עבודה זרה become forbidden while a גוי holds it? רב נחמן says it is permitted. After one proof falls, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about a גוי repaying a debt. רב ששת explains that the forbidden case there is because the Jew wants the idol preserved. A challenge from a convert's inheritance is finally answered by רב פפא: the חכמים were specially lenient with a גר's inheritance.

steps.title: The ברייתא allows helping to uproot כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא: a person may help uproot כלאים, because that reduces the wrongdoing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may uproot the כלאים together with him, in order to reduce the wrongdoing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that began earlier. Tending כלאים is not allowed, but helping to pull them out is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling out כלאים does not help them grow. It gets rid of a forbidden mixture, so it lessens the wrong. This line is the base text that the rest of this section analyzes.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden mixtures of seeds planted together

phrases.english: but one may uproot with him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the person named earlier in the ברייתא, a non-Jew working the field. "Uproot" means pulling out the כלאים.

phrases.english: in order to reduce the impropriety.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Helping to uproot כלאים is permitted because it reduces the wrongdoing.

steps.title: The ברייתא is assumed to follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who says that even someone who keeps כלאים in his field gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed: whose view is this? It is רבי עקיבא's, who says that one who keeps כלאים gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא and assumes it was רבי עקיבא. This sets up the point that the permission to uproot holds even by the strictest view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא forbids even passively leaving כלאים in place. If the ברייתא still allows uprooting by his view, the permission is strong. The word סברוה signals that this is the first assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: one who keeps or leaves something in place

phrases.english: They assumed: whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Akiva's,
who says: one who maintains diverse kinds is flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose view the ברייתא from step 1 follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, even keeping כלאים earns lashes, and the ברייתא is assumed to follow him.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that weeding or covering כלאים earns lashes, and רבי עקיבא adds that even keeping them does.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: one who weeds or covers כלאים gets lashes. רבי עקיבא says: even one who keeps them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for what it just said about רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gives lashes only for active work, like weeding or covering seeds with earth. רבי עקיבא goes further and gives lashes even for doing nothing and letting the כלאים stay.

keyTerms.meaning: one who covers seeds with earth

phrases.english: As it is taught: one who weeds or covers
diverse kinds is flogged,
Rabbi Akiva says: even one who maintains them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim about רבי עקיבא in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא gives lashes even for keeping כלאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a dispute about lashes for כלאים.

steps.title: What is רבי עקיבא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא learns that keeping כלאים is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי עקיבא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי עקיבא's view. This sets up the answer from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק speaks about sowing. So the גמרא wants to know how רבי עקיבא extends it to someone who only keeps the plants in his field.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for forbidding someone to keep כלאים.

steps.title: Learning "keeping" from the wording of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק literally speaks about sowing, but the words "לא כלאים" teach that no כלאים may be in the field at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, "Your field you shall not sow with כלאים." That covers only sowing. Where do we learn about keeping them? The words "not... כלאים" teach it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא reads extra meaning into the פסוק's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read in order, the פסוק only forbids sowing. Reading the words "לא כלאים" on their own gives a wider rule: there must be no כלאים in your field. That forbids keeping them too.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Your field you shall not sow with diverse kinds,"
I have only one who sows;
from where do we know one who maintains?
The verse teaches: "Not... diverse kinds."
phrases.notes: Read these two words by themselves: there should be no כלאים in your field at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "לא כלאים" in the פסוק forbid having כלאים in the field at all, so keeping them is forbidden too.

steps.title: Even רבי עקיבא allows acting to reduce wrongdoing
steps.stepSummary: Even though רבי עקיבא forbids keeping כלאים, uprooting them to reduce wrongdoing is permitted. This supports רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet to reduce wrongdoing, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its first proof for רב נחמן: even by רבי עקיבא's strict view, acting to reduce wrongdoing is allowed. The next step will challenge this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא forbids even leaving כלאים in place. If he still allows someone to keep them for a short time in order to uproot them, then reducing wrongdoing is clearly allowed. The same reasoning lets a person be paid for breaking barrels of יין נסך, as רב נחמן ruled.
steps.whatToRemember: This first proof depends on the ברייתא following רבי עקיבא. Step 7 questions that, and step 10 shows the support for רב נחמן holds anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that work which gets rid of a forbidden thing, rather than helping it, is allowed, even when payment is involved.

phrases.english: Yet to reduce impropriety, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's strict view from steps 2 to 5 to strengthen the permission in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Acting to reduce wrongdoing is permitted even by רבי עקיבא's view, which supports רב נחמן.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב נחמן by saying the ברייתא could follow the רבנן instead of רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back the proof it just brought for רב נחמן. It suggests the ברייתא follows the רבנן, not רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן punish active work like weeding or covering כלאים, but they allow simply keeping them in the field. So uprooting כלאים with a גוי tells us nothing about removing something that is truly forbidden to keep, and the proof for רב נחמן falls away.

phrases.english: No, whose [opinion] is this?
phrases.notes: "This" means the ברייתא about uprooting כלאים together with a גוי.

phrases.english: It is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רב נחמן reached in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could follow the רבנן, who allow keeping כלאים, so it says nothing about removing something forbidden.

steps.title: Why would the רבנן mention only uprooting?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows the רבנן, why does it permit only uprooting, when even keeping כלאים is allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows the רבנן, why does it single out uprooting? Even keeping the כלאים is perfectly fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new suggestion. According to the רבנן, there would be no reason to mention uprooting specially.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן allow keeping כלאים in the field. So even leaving them in place should be allowed, not just uprooting them. The ברייתא's narrow wording does not fit the רבנן.

phrases.english: If [it is] the Rabbis,
why specifically uprooting?
Even keeping [them] is also fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 7 that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן allow even keeping כלאים, so limiting the permission to uprooting makes no sense for them.

steps.title: The case is unpaid work, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about someone who helps the גוי for free. It follows רבי יהודה, who forbids giving a גוי a free gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? One where he works without pay. This follows רבי יהודה, who said that giving them a free gift is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The problem in the ברייתא is not the כלאים themselves but working for the גוי for free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Free work for a גוי counts as a free gift, which רבי יהודה forbids. Only uprooting is allowed because it lessens wrongdoing. Keeping the plants for him for free would just be a forbidden gift.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's ban here is about giving a free gift to a גוי. It is not about כלאים. That is a separate topic that explains why only uprooting is mentioned.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he works for free,
and it is רבי יהודה, who said:
to give them a free gift is forbidden.
phrases.notes: "Them" means גוים. Free work for a גוי counts as a free gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן דְּקָא עָבֵיד בְּחִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (unpaid work) and identifying the author (רבי יהודה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's focus on uprooting makes no sense according to the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is unpaid help. Only uprooting is allowed, since any other free help would be a forbidden gift.

steps.title: From רבי יהודה we learn רבי עקיבא too, so רב נחמן is supported
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids free gifts but allows helping when it lessens wrongdoing. In the same way, רבי עקיבא would allow uprooting כלאים to lessen wrongdoing. So רב נחמן is supported after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: From רבי יהודה we can learn about רבי עקיבא. Doesn't רבי יהודה say a free gift to them is forbidden, but lessening wrongdoing is fine? So too for רבי עקיבא: even though he says one who keeps כלאים gets lashes, lessening wrongdoing is fine. And there is nothing more to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around to bring back the proof for רב נחמן. Then it closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יהודה, who forbids free gifts, allows the free uprooting because it lessens wrongdoing. By the same reasoning, רבי עקיבא, who forbids keeping כלאים, still allows uprooting with a גוי to lessen wrongdoing. That is just what רב נחמן says.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more (the discussion is closed)

steps.whatToRemember: Doing something to lessen wrongdoing is allowed, even according to the strict opinions of רבי יהודה (free gifts) and רבי עקיבא (keeping כלאים). This supports רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule of reducing wrongdoing holds even for the strictest views, which makes רב נחמן's ruling stronger.

phrases.english: From רבי יהודה we can learn about רבי עקיבא,
didn't רבי יהודה say:
it is forbidden to give them a free gift,
but to lessen wrongdoing is fine.
According to רבי עקיבא also,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: even though רבי עקיבא said:
one who keeps כלאים gets lashes,
to lessen wrongdoing is fine.
And nothing more [to say].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 9 to bring back the support for רב נחמן that step 7 had rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Lessening wrongdoing is permitted even according to רבי עקיבא, so the ברייתא supports רב נחמן.

steps.title: Does money from idol worship become forbidden in a gentile's hand?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: when a גוי sells an object of עבודה זרה, does the forbidden status pass to the money in his hand?
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat again and asked: the money from עבודה זרה that is in a גוי's hand, what is the law? Does the forbidden status pass to its money in a גוי's hand, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a brand-new topic. The sages ask whether money from selling עבודה זרה is forbidden even when a גוי holds it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know עבודה זרה can pass its forbidden status to the money it is sold for. The question is whether this happens only when the money is in a Jew's hand, or even when it is in a גוי's hand. This sets up the discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Passes its forbidden status to its money

phrases.english: They sat again and they asked:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיַד גּוֹי, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Money of idol worship in a gentile's hand, what is [the law]?
Does it pass [its status] to its money in a gentile's hand,
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the closing of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether עבודה זרה makes the money it is sold for forbidden even when a גוי holds that money.

steps.title: רב נחמן's proof from רבה בר אבוה's advice to converts
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the money is permitted. He points to רבה בר אבוה, who told גוים who wanted to convert to first sell everything they owned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It makes sense that money from selling עבודה זרה, while in a גוי's hand, is permitted. We see this from the people who came to רבה בר אבוה. He told them: Go sell everything you have, and then come convert. Why? Because he holds that money from עבודה זרה in a גוי's hand is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question from step 11: the money is permitted. He proves it from a story about רבה בר אבוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These גוים surely owned idols. רבה בר אבוה told them to sell everything, idols included, and then convert. That suggests he held they could keep using the money after converting. That only works if the money never became forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it stands to reason
Money received from selling an object of idol worship

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them:
It stands to reason that the money from idol worship
while in a gentile's hand is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּהָנְהוּ דַּאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: as we see from those who came before Rabba bar Avuh,
phrases.notes: These were גוים who came wanting to convert.

phrases.english: he said to them: Go sell
everything that you have,
and then come and convert.
What is the reason?
Because he holds:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיַד גּוֹי מוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: money from idol worship in a gentile's hand is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּמֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיַד גּוֹי מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 11 and brings a proof.
steps.raayaObject: Money from selling עבודה זרה in a גוי's hand is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר אבוה's instruction to future converts to sell all their belongings before converting.

steps.title: The converts' case is different because they cancelled their idols
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Someone who plans to convert surely cancels his idols first, so he is not selling real עבודה זרה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe that case is different. Since they planned to convert, they certainly cancelled the idol's status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof. It says the story of the converts does not prove anything about ordinary עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי can cancel (בטל) his idol's forbidden status. People about to convert have obviously rejected their idols, so what they sold was no longer עבודה זרה. That means the story says nothing about money from a real idol.

keyTerms.meaning: He cancelled it (removed its idol status)

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since his intention is to convert,
he certainly cancelled it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not reject רב נחמן's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The converts had cancelled their idols, so the items sold were no longer עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A new proof from a ברייתא about a גוי repaying a debt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא covers a גוי who owes a Jew money. If the גוי sold עבודה זרה and then paid, the money is permitted. If he asked the Jew to wait until he sells it, the money is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof comes from here. A Jew was owed a מנה by a גוי. The גוי sold עבודה זרה and brought him the money, or sold יין נסך and brought him the money: it is permitted. But if the גוי said, "Wait for me until I sell עבודה זרה and I will bring it to you," or "until I sell יין נסך and I will bring it to you," it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first proof failed, the גמרא brings a different source to support רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the Jew receives money that came straight from selling a real idol, and it is permitted. That supports the idea that the money is not forbidden while it is in the גוי's hand. The second case, where it is forbidden, will need an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, the proof is from here
A sum of one hundred דינרים
Wine poured as an offering to an idol

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve the same sale and the same money. The only difference is whether the Jew was told ahead of time that his payment depends on the idol being sold.

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from here:
A Jew who was owed one hundred dinars by a gentile,
and the gentile sold idol worship and brought him the money,
or sold libation wine and brought him the money: it is permitted,
but if he said to him:
"Wait for me until I sell idol worship
and I will bring it to you,"
or "until I sell libation wine and I will bring it to you": it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 13 with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Money from selling עבודה זרה in a גוי's hand is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first clause (רישא) of the ברייתא, where the debt repaid from idol money is permitted.

steps.title: Why are the two halves of the ברייתא different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the money is permitted in the first case but forbidden in the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first case, and what is different about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two halves of the ברייתא seem to clash, and asks what separates them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both halves the גוי sells עבודה זרה and pays the Jew with the money. If idol money in a גוי's hand is permitted, the second half should be permitted too. The גמרא needs a reason that explains only the second half.

phrases.english: What is different about the first clause
and what is different about the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ברייתא from step 14 can hold together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same kind of money is permitted in one clause and forbidden in the other, so a distinguishing reason is needed.

steps.title: רב ששת: in the second case the Jew wants the idol to survive
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains the second half. The Jew knows his payment depends on the idol being sold, so he wants it kept intact. That is why the money is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: In the last case it is forbidden because the Jew becomes like someone who wants the idol to be preserved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. The second half is forbidden for a special reason, not because idol money is forbidden in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the גוי says "wait until I sell it," the Jew is now hoping the idol stays whole so it can be sold. Wanting an idol to be preserved is forbidden. In the first case the Jew had no such stake, so the money is permitted. That supports רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Wants it to continue existing (be preserved)

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew may accept payment from a גוי out of money that came from selling עבודה זרה. But if he was told his payment depends on the idol being sold, it is forbidden, because then he wants the idol to survive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This separates two issues: the money itself, which is permitted while in the גוי's hand, and the Jew's attitude toward the idol, which can make it forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
The last clause is forbidden because he becomes
like one who wants it preserved.
phrases.notes: The Jew hopes the idol stays whole so it can be sold and he gets paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: סֵיפָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּי רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the second clause has an extra reason to forbid it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two clauses seem to contradict each other about idol money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second clause is forbidden only because the Jew wants the idol preserved. The first clause stands as proof that idol money in a גוי's hand is permitted.

steps.title: A challenge from the convert who inherits with his gentile brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether wanting an object kept intact really makes it forbidden. It points to a משנה where a גר may swap his share of the idols and יין נסך for money and produce, even though he seems to want them preserved until the swap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really forbidden just because he wants it to stay intact? We learned in a משנה: a convert and a gentile inherited from their gentile father. The convert may say, 'You take the idols and I'll take the money,' or 'You take the libation wine and I'll take the produce.' But once the property has come into the convert's possession, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's reason from the last step. It brings a משנה where wanting the idol kept intact does not seem to make anything forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the estate is divided, the גר needs the idols and the wine to stay whole, because that is what lets him trade them for an equal share of money and produce. Even so, the משנה allows the trade. That seems to show that רוצה בקיומו alone does not make the money forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He wants it to stay intact and keep existing
Wine poured or used for idol worship; it is forbidden to benefit from it

phrases.english: And if he wants it to stay intact
in a case like this, is it forbidden?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
A convert and a gentile who inherited from their gentile father,
the convert may say to him:
"You take the idols, and I will take the money,"
"You take the libation wine, and I will take the produce";
but if this is after it came into the convert's possession, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא מִי אֲסִיר? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's reason from step 16 that wanting the idol preserved makes the money forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's principle that רוצה בקיומו makes the money forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before the division, the גר wants the idols and wine kept whole so he can trade them for an equal share, yet the משנה permits the trade.

steps.title: The idol keeps its value even in broken pieces
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר עולא says the משנה is talking about an idol made of material that stays valuable even when it is smashed. Because of that, the גר does not care whether it stays whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר עולא said: The משנה is talking about an idol that keeps its value even when it is broken into pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר עולא defends רב ששת by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the idol is made of something like precious metal, its pieces are worth as much as the whole statue. So the גר does not need it to stay intact, and this case is not רוצה בקיומו at all. רב ששת's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (here, the משנה just quoted)
It can be divided by its broken pieces; its value stays even when broken

phrases.english: רבא בר עולא said:
The משנה is talking about an idol
that can be divided by its broken pieces.
phrases.notes: He means the broken pieces are worth the same as the whole idol, so smashing it loses nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא: מַתְנִיתִין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַמִּתְחַלֶּקֶת לְפִי שְׁבָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by limiting the משנה to a specific kind of idol.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גר wants the idol kept intact, yet the trade is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The idol stays valuable in pieces, so the גר does not care about keeping it whole.

steps.title: That answer doesn't work for the wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the answer works for idols but not for יין נסך. Wine has no 'broken pieces' that keep their value.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for the idol, but what can you say about the libation wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא בר עולא's answer, because the משנה also mentions יין נסך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wine spills, it is simply gone. So the גר must want the wine kept safe until the trade, and the original problem comes back for the wine half of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out fine (for this part)
What is there to say? (what answer works here?)

phrases.english: That works for the idol,
but about libation wine, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, יֵין נֶסֶךְ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 18 as incomplete, since it does not cover the wine case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר עולא's answer about idols that keep their value when broken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wine cannot stay valuable once it is spilled or lost, so the גר must want it preserved.

steps.title: The wine case is about חרס הדרייני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the wine in the משנה is wine soaked into חרס הדרייני. The clay can be broken and the wine is still there in it, so the גר does not need the vessel kept whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about Hadrianic earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves רבא בר עולא's approach by finding a type of wine that also keeps its value when broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חרס הדרייני is clay that has soaked up wine. The wine is still in the clay even if it is broken into pieces. So, like the idol, the גר does not care whether it stays whole.

keyTerms.meaning: Hadrianic earthenware: clay pieces soaked with wine, from which the wine can later be brought out

phrases.english: It is talking about Hadrianic earthenware.
phrases.notes: This is clay soaked in wine. Later you soak it in water to get the wine back, so breaking it loses nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by applying the same 'value survives breaking' idea to the wine.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine must be kept intact or it is lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine soaked into clay keeps its value even when the clay breaks.

steps.title: He still wants it kept from theft and loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the whole 'broken pieces' approach. Even if breaking does not matter, the גר still wants the items not to be stolen or lost before the trade, and that is wanting them preserved.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't he still want it preserved, so that it won't be stolen and won't be lost?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבא בר עולא's whole line of answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wanting something kept intact is not only about breaking. If the idol or the clay were stolen or lost, the גר would lose its value in the trade. So he is still רוצה בקיומו, and the challenge from the משנה returns.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (introduces a strong objection)
That they should not be stolen and not be lost

phrases.english: But doesn't he want it preserved,
so that they won't be stolen and won't be lost!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יִגָּנֵובוּ וְשֶׁלֹּא יֵאָבֵדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the answers of steps 18 and 20 together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the גר does not care whether the items are preserved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if breaking does not matter, theft or loss would still hurt him, so he does want them preserved.

steps.title: A convert's inheritance is a special leniency
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. A convert's inheritance is different, because the חכמים were lenient with it so the convert would not return to his old ways. For anyone else, wanting the idol preserved does make the money forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: You are bringing a proof from a convert's inheritance? A convert's inheritance is different, because the חכמים were lenient with it. This was a decree, so that he would not go back to his corrupt ways.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא drops the earlier answers and explains that the convert's case is a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא agrees that the גר does want the items preserved. Even so, the חכמים made a special leniency for him, so that losing his inheritance would not push him back to idol worship. That means the משנה cannot disprove רב ששת's general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule made by the חכמים to protect against a problem
He will go back to his corrupt ways

steps.whatToRemember: The convert's inheritance is a unique leniency, so it does not break רב ששת's rule. In ordinary cases, money that depends on an idol staying intact is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רב ששת's rule in place as the general הלכה. The convert's case becomes a special exception made to protect new converts.

phrases.english: Rather, רב פפא said:
You are bringing up a convert's inheritance?
A convert's inheritance is different,
because the Sages were lenient with it,
as a decree, so that he would not go back to his corrupt ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: יְרוּשַּׁת הַגֵּר קָאָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי יְרוּשַּׁת הַגֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 21 rejects רבא בר עולא's approach, רב פפא answers the challenge of step 17 in a completely different way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The convert case shows that wanting an item preserved does not make it forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The convert's inheritance is a special leniency of the חכמים, so רב ששת's general rule stands.
